entities.label: Company
entities.description: A company the workspace deals with — a customer, a supplier, a partner, an investor or a holding. The canonical record: an invoice, a deal and a timesheet all point at THIS row rather than each app keeping its own spelling of the name.

entities.label: Contact
entities.description: A person at an organization we deal with. EXTERNAL people only — colleagues come from the platform people directory, and leads, candidates and applicants belong to the app that runs that process.

entities.label: Research run
entities.description: One automatic research run: what it looked at, what it wrote, what it cost, and how it ended. Kept with the organization so a failure is visible on the record, not only in an admin table.

entities.label: Source
entities.description: A page the research actually read. Every promoted fact points at one of these, so any number on the record can be traced back to where it came from.

entities.label: Run document
entities.description: Which documents one run actually read, and which of them reached the model. A source is shared across every run that saw it, so the source row itself cannot say which run used it - that is what this join carries. It is also the only record of the corpus a fact was checked against: 'did the model actually see this page' becomes a query instead of a guess.

entities.label: Fact
entities.description: Where a single promoted value came from: the quote, the source, the confidence, and whether it was applied. Superseded rows are kept so the record shows WHY a value changed.

entities.label: Funding round
entities.description: A funding event. The latest of these is rolled up onto the organization in code - the model is never asked for both the rounds and a summary of the rounds, because the two would disagree.

entities.label: Investor
entities.description: A firm or person that put money into this company. Its own entity rather than a comma-separated string on the record, because an investor is something somebody wants to CLICK - a name alone means opening a search engine, and that is the difference between a record that answers a question and one that just displays a fact. Shared across rounds: a fund that led the Seed and followed the Series A is one investor with two rounds, not two rows.

entities.label: Channel
entities.description: Where this company publishes: its blog, press page, YouTube channel, LinkedIn page. Discovered from links on the company's OWN site, which is what makes them trustworthy - a channel found by searching a company name is a guess wearing a link. Discovery only: nothing here is polled yet, and a channel never changes a value on the record.

entities.label: Officer
entities.description: A person the commercial register or the legal notice DECLARES in a role: a managing director, a board member, an authorized signatory. Deliberately not a contact - a contact is somebody you deal with and curate, this is a researched claim about the company. Name and role only: a model that half-remembers a director will invent an email address with total confidence, and an invented address for a real named person is the one error here with a victim. Promoting an officer to a contact is a human action.

entities.label: Post
entities.description: Something this company published: a blog post, a press release, a video. Read from the channel's own feed. Monitoring output, not research - a post is a dated item with a link, and it never changes a value on the record.

entities.label: Correction
entities.description: A human correcting a researched value. While one is active the writer never overwrites that field, and keeps refreshing every other one. This is also what makes a correction RATE countable rather than something inferred from history.

dependencies.why: Every contact here is also a person in People

actions.label: Research now
actions.description: Look this company up on the public web and file what is found alongside - never over - what you typed.

actions.label: Refresh
actions.description: Research this company again even though it was looked up recently. Ordinary research is refused inside the freshness window so nobody can run up a bill by pressing a button five times; this is the deliberate way past it.
